**Surah al-Nasr is Meccan** [[Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "(When the help of Allah comes, and the conquest) was revealed in Medina." Ibn Mardawayh also related from Ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "(When the help of Allah comes) was revealed in Medina." Ibn Jarir related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar that he said: "(When the help of Allah comes, and the conquest) was revealed entirely in Medina, after the conquest of Mecca and the entry of people into the religion, announcing to him the end of his life." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/658.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿When the help of Allah comes, and the conquest﴾ He means the conquest of Mecca.

The account of it, as related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq and the scholars of narratives, is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a treaty with Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyah, and they agreed to suspend hostilities between people for ten years, during which people would be safe and would refrain from one another, and that whoever wished to enter into the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could enter it, and whoever wished to enter into the covenant and pact of Quraysh could enter it, then Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh, and Khuza'ah entered into the pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There had been an old enmity between them.

Then Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'ah while they were at a water source of theirs at the bottom of Mecca called "al-Watir." Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Du'ali went out with the clan of al-Du'il from Banu Bakr and launched a night attack on Khuza'ah, though not all of Banu Bakr followed him. They killed a man from them, and they fought and battled. Quraysh supplied Banu Bakr with weapons, and some of Quraysh fought alongside them secretly at night, until they drove Khuza'ah back into the sanctuary. Among those from Quraysh who helped Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah that night, disguised, were Safwan ibn Umayya, Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn Amr, together with their slaves. When they reached the sanctuary, Banu Bakr said: "O Nawfal, we have entered the sanctuary! Your god, your god!" Nawfal said a grave word: "Indeed, there is no god for me today! O Banu Bakr, take your revenge here."

When Quraysh backed Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, and they inflicted harm on them and broke what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the covenant, by permitting what they had made lawful against Khuza'ah, who were within his covenant, 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i set out and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina. This was among the things that stirred up the conquest of Mecca. He stood before him while he was sitting in the mosque among the people, and said:

"O Allah, I appeal to Muhammad...
the alliance of our father and his, the ancient one.
Indeed Quraysh have broken the promise to you,
and violated your firm covenant."

The verses are as we mentioned in Surah al-Tawba [[See Ibn Hisham's Sira for the full meaning: 4/9-10.]].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have been helped, O 'Amr ibn Salim!" Then a cloud appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the sky, and he said: "Indeed this cloud is flashing with lightning, bringing the victory of Banu Ka'b," and they were the kin of 'Amr ibn Salim.

Then Budayl ibn Warqa' set out with a group from Khuza'ah until they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what had been inflicted upon them, and of the support [[i.e., the assistance]] Quraysh gave Banu Bakr against them. Then they returned to Mecca. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to the people: "It is as if I see Abu Sufyan has come to strengthen the covenant and extend the period."

Budayl ibn Warqa' went on and met Abu Sufyan at 'Usfan. Quraysh had sent him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to strengthen the covenant and extend the period, for they feared what they had done. When Abu Sufyan met Budayl, he said: "Where have you come from, O Budayl?" He thought that he had gone to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Budayl said: "I traveled among Khuza'ah along this coast and through the bottom of this valley." Abu Sufyan said: "Did you not go to Muhammad?" He said: "No." When Budayl returned to Mecca, Abu Sufyan said: "If he had come to Medina, he would have fed his camel dates there." So he went to the place where Budayl's camel had kneeled, took some of its dung, broke it apart, and saw date pits in it. He said: "I swear by Allah, Budayl has indeed gone to Muhammad!"

Then Abu Sufyan set out until he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina. He entered upon his daughter Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan, and when he went to sit on the bedding of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she folded it up away from him. He said: "O my daughter, have you turned away from me in favor of this bedding, or have you turned it away from me?" She said: "Rather, it is the bedding of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you are a polytheist, unclean. I did not want you to sit on the bedding of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "By Allah, indeed, O my daughter, evil has befallen you since I left you." Then he went out until he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke with him, but he did not answer him at all [except that he said: "The people of Mecca have broken the covenant"] [[What is between the parentheses is omitted from "B."]].

Then he went to Abu Bakr and asked him to speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his behalf. He said: "I will not do that." Then he came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and spoke with him, and he said: "Should I intercede for you with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?! By Allah, even if I found nothing but ants, I would fight you with them!" Then he went out and entered upon 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. With him was Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and with her was al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, a boy crawling between her hands. He said: "O 'Ali, indeed you are the closest of the people to me in kinship, and the nearest of them to me in relationship. I have come on a need, so do not let me return as I came, disappointed. Intercede for us with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Ali said: "Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has resolved upon a matter about which we cannot speak to him." So he turned to Fatima and said: "O daughter of Muhammad, would you command this son of yours to give protection between the people, so that he would be the lord of the Arabs until the end of time?" She said: "By Allah, my son has not reached the age to give protection between people, and no one gives protection against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "O Abu al-Hasan, indeed I see that matters have become severe for me, so advise me." He said: "By Allah, I know of nothing that will benefit you, but you are the lord of Banu Kinana. So stand up and give protection between the people, then go back to your land." He said: "Do you think that will benefit me at all?" He said: "No, by Allah, I do not think so, but I do not find any other course for you."

Abu Sufyan stood up in the mosque and said: "O people, indeed I have given protection between the people." Then he mounted his camel and set off. When he came to Quraysh, they said: "What is behind you?" He said: "I went to Muhammad and spoke with him, but by Allah, he did not answer me at all. Then I went to Ibn Abi Quhafa (Abu Bakr), and I found no good in him. Then I went to Ibn al-Khattab, and I found him the most hostile of the people. Then I went to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and I found him the gentlest of the people, and he advised me to do something, which I have done, but by Allah, I do not know whether it will benefit me at all or not." They said: "And what did he command you?" He said: "He commanded me to give protection between the people, so I did." They said: "Did Muhammad (ﷺ) approve of that?" He said: "No." They said: "By Allah, 'Ali has only made a fool of you, so what you said will not benefit us." He said: "No, by Allah, I found nothing other than that."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the people to prepare for the march, and commanded his family to equip him. Abu Bakr entered upon his daughter 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, while she was arranging some of the equipment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "O my daughter, has the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded you to equip him?" She said: "Yes, so prepare." He said: "Where do you think he is heading?" She said: "I do not know." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed the people that he was setting out for Mecca, and commanded them to be diligent and ready. He said: "O Allah, seize the spies and the news from Quraysh, until we surprise them in their lands." So the people prepared.

Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a wrote a letter to Quraysh [in which there is a story] [[Omitted from "B."]] which we mentioned in Surah al-Mumtahana [[See above: 8/91.]].

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed Abu Rihm Kulthum ibn Husayn ibn Khalaf al-Ghifari as his deputy over Medina, and he set out intending Mecca, ten days into Ramadan of the year eight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fasted, and the people fasted with him, until when he reached al-Kadid, a water source between 'Usfan and Amaj, he broke his fast.

Then he went on until he halted at Marr al-Zahran with ten thousand Muslims, and none of the Muhajirun or the Ansar stayed behind from him. When he halted at Marr al-Zahran, news about Quraysh had become obscured, and no news from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached them, and they did not know what he was going to do. That night Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Hakim ibn Hizam, and Budayl ibn Warqa' went out, searching for news to see whether they could find any. Al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib said that night: "Woe to the morning of Quraysh! By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) surprises them in their lands and enters Mecca by force, it will be the destruction of Quraysh until the end of time."

Al-'Abbas went out on the mule of the Messenger of Allah and said: "I will go out to al-Arak. Perhaps I will see a woodcutter, or a milk-seller, or someone entering Mecca, who will inform them of the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they come to him and seek safe-conduct from him before he enters it upon them by force."

Al-Abbas said: "I went out, and by Allah I was wandering among the arak trees looking for what I had come out for, when I heard the voices of Abu Sufyan, Hakim ibn Hizam and Badil ibn Warqa'. They had come out to seek news. I heard Abu Sufyan saying: 'By Allah, I have never seen fires like tonight's.' Badil said: 'By Allah, these are the fires of Khuza'ah, [whom] war [has] burned' [[Aharaqathā.]]. Abu Sufyan said: 'Khuza'ah are too base and too humble for that.' I recognised his voice and said: 'O Abu Hanzalah!' He recognised my voice and said: 'O Abu al-Fadl!' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What is wrong with you? May my father and mother be your ransom!' I said: 'Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! By Allah, this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who has come with what you cannot withstand, with ten thousand Muslims.' He said: 'What is the way out?' I said: 'By Allah, if he gets hold of you he will surely cut off your neck. So mount behind me on this mule, and I will bring you to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that you may seek safe-conduct from him.' He rode behind me, and his two companions turned back. I set off riding the mule of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Every time I passed a fire of the Muslims, they looked at me and said: 'This is the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' Then I passed the fire of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: 'Who is this?' He stood up towards me, and when he saw Abu Sufyan on the back of the animal, he said: 'Abu Sufyan, the enemy of Allah! Praise be to Allah, who has delivered you into our hands without any treaty or pact.' Then he ran towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I urged the mule on and outpaced him, as a slow animal outpaces a slow man. I jumped down from the mule and entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Umar entered after me. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is Abu Sufyan, the enemy of Allah. Allah has delivered him into our hands without any treaty or pact, so let me strike off his neck.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have granted him protection.' Then I sat down beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), took hold of his head, and said: 'By Allah, none shall converse with him tonight except me.' When Umar kept pressing about him, I said: 'Gently, O Umar! By Allah, you do this only because he is a man of the Banu Abd Manaf. Had he been of the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b, you would not have said this.' He said: 'Gently, O Abbas! By Allah, your Islam on the day you embraced it was dearer to me than the Islam of al-Khattab, had he embraced it. [That is because I know that your Islam was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than the Islam of al-Khattab, had he embraced it.] [[What is between the brackets is omitted in manuscript B.]]' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Take him, O Abbas, to your lodging, and when morning comes, bring him to me.' He said: 'I went to my lodging and he spent the night with me. When morning came, I went with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he saw him, he said: "Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! Has the time not come for you to know that there is no god but Allah?"' He said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom! How forbearing you are, how noble and how kind! By Allah, I had thought that if there were another god with Allah, it would have availed me something by now.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! Has the time not come for you to know that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom! How forbearing you are, how noble and how kind! As for this matter, there is still something in my soul about it [until now] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]].' Al-Abbas said: 'I said to him: "Woe to you! Embrace Islam and testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, before your neck is struck off."' He said: 'So he bore witness to the truth and embraced Islam.' Al-Abbas said: 'I said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a man who loves this glory, so grant him something."' He said: 'Yes. Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever closes his door is safe, and whoever enters the mosque is safe.' When he turned to leave, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Abbas, detain him at the narrow part of the valley, at the nose [of the mountain] [[The projecting end of the mountain, a thing that projects and narrows the path.]], until the armies of Allah pass by him and he sees them.' He said: 'So I went out with him and detained him where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded me.'

He said: 'The tribes passed by him with their banners. Each time a tribe passed, he said: "Who are these, O Abbas?" I would say: "Sulaym." He would say: "What have I to do with Sulaym?" Then another tribe would pass and he would say: "Who are these?" I would say: "Muzaynah." He would say: "What have I to do with Muzaynah?" Until the tribes were exhausted; no tribe passed but he asked me about it, and when I told him, he would say: "What have I to do with the Banu so-and-so?" until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by in the al-Khadra' [the green battalion], the battalion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in which were the Emigrants and the Helpers, of whom nothing could be seen but the eyes from the iron [armour]. He said: "Glory be to Allah! Who are these, O Abbas?" I said: "This is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the Emigrants and the Helpers." He said: "By Allah, no one has the strength or the power to stand against these. By Allah, O Abu al-Fadl, the kingdom of your nephew has become mighty." I said: "Woe to you! It is prophethood." He said: "Yes, then."

I said: "Now go to your people and warn them." So he set off quickly until he reached Makkah, and he shouted in the mosque at the top of his voice: "O assembly of Quraysh! Muhammad has come to you with what you cannot withstand!" They said: "Then what?" He said: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe." They said: "Woe to you! What use is your house to us?" He said: "And whoever enters the mosque is safe, and whoever closes his door is safe." So the people dispersed to their houses and to the mosque.

He said: "Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa' came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Marr al-Zahran, and they embraced Islam and pledged allegiance to him. When they had pledged allegiance, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent them ahead of him to Quraysh to call them to Islam."

When Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa' left the Prophet (ﷺ) intending for Makkah, he sent al-Zubayr after them, gave him his banner, and appointed him over the cavalry of the Emigrants and the Helpers. He commanded him to plant his banner at the top of Makkah, at al-Hujun, and said: "Do not leave the place where I have ordered you to plant my banner until I come to you." From there the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah, and his tent was pitched there. He commanded Khalid ibn al-Walid, with those among Qudaʿah and Banu Sulaym who had embraced Islam, to enter from the lower part of Makkah, where the Banu Bakr were, whom Quraysh had mobilised, along with the Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf and those of the Ahabish. Quraysh had ordered them to be in the lower part of Makkah. Safwan ibn Umayyah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Suhayl ibn Amr had gathered some people at al-Khandamah to fight. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Khalid and al-Zubayr when he sent them: "Do not fight except those who fight you." He ordered Sa'd ibn Ubadah to enter with some of the people from Kada'. Sa'd, as he set out entering, said: "Today is the day of slaughter; today the sanctity is made lawful." A man of the Emigrants heard this and said: "O Messenger of Allah, listen to what Sa'd ibn Ubadah has said, and we are not sure that he will not have a powerful attack upon Quraysh." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Go to him and take the banner from him, and you be the one who enters with it." Thus there was no fighting in the upper part of Makkah from the side of al-Zubayr. As for Khalid ibn al-Walid, he confronted Quraysh, the Banu Bakr and the Ahabish in the lower part of Makkah, fought them, and Allah routed them. There was no other fighting in Makkah apart from that.

About twelve or thirteen of the polytheists were killed, and none of the Muslims was killed except a man of Juhaynah called Salamah ibn al-Mayla', from the horsemen of Khalid ibn al-Walid, and two men called Kurz ibn Jabir [and Khunays] [[In manuscript A it is Hunays, and in manuscript B Khubaysh; the text here follows Ibn Hisham.]] ibn Khalid, who were in the cavalry of Khalid ibn al-Walid. They strayed from him and took a path other than his, and both were killed.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had instructed his Muslim commanders, when he sent them to enter Makkah, not to fight anyone except those who fought them, except [that he had instructed] concerning a group whom he named, whom he commanded to be killed even if they were found clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah. Among them was Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh. He had commanded his killing because he had embraced Islam and then apostatised to polytheism. He fled to Uthman, who was his foster brother, and Uthman hid him until he brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after the people of Makkah had become secure, and he sought safe-conduct for him. [And Abdullah ibn Khatal, a man of the Banu Tamim ibn Ghalib] [[What is between the brackets is omitted in manuscript A.]]. He had commanded his killing because he had been a Muslim, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him as a collector of alms. He had a freedman who served him, and he was a Muslim. He stopped at a station and commanded the freedman to slaughter a goat for him and prepare food for him, then he slept. When he woke, nothing had been prepared for him, so he attacked the freedman and killed him, then he apostatised to polytheism. He had two singing slave-girls who sang satire against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he commanded that they be killed along with him. Also Huwayrith ibn [Nuqayd] [[In manuscript B it is Nufayr.]] ibn Wahb, who was among those who harassed him in Makkah. Also Miqyas ibn Sababah; he commanded his killing because he had killed the Helper who had accidentally killed his brother, and because he returned to Quraysh as an apostate. Also Sarrah, a freedwoman who belonged to some of the Banu al-Muttalib, who was among those who harassed him in Makkah. And Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl: as for Ikrimah, he fled to Yemen, and his wife Umm Hakim bint al-Harith ibn Hisham embraced Islam and sought safe-conduct for him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he granted it to him. She went out in pursuit of him until she brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he embraced Islam.

As for Abdullah ibn Khatal, Sa'd ibn Hurayth al-Makhzumi and Abu Barzah al-Aslami killed him, both sharing in his blood. As for Miqyas ibn Sababah, Tumaylah ibn Abdullah, a man of his own people, killed him. As for the two slave-girls of Ibn Khatal, one of them was killed and the other fled until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked to grant her safe-conduct, and he granted it. As for Sarrah, she hid until safe-conduct was sought for her, and he granted it, and she lived until a man among the people trampled her with his horse in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab in al-Abtah, and killed her. As for Huwayrith ibn Nuqayd, Ali ibn Abi Talib killed him.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah, he stood at the door of the Ka'bah and said: "There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, He supported His servant, and He defeated the confederates alone. Every glory, blood or wealth claimed in the Jahiliyyah is under these two feet of mine, except the custody of the House and the provision of water for the pilgrims. O assembly of Quraysh, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its boasting in ancestors. People are from Adam, and Adam was created from dust." Then he recited: ﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], to the end of the verse. "O people of Makkah, what do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set them free, although Allah had given him power over their necks by force. Therefore the people of Makkah were called the Freed Ones (al-Tulaqa').

Then the people gathered for the pledge of allegiance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat for them on al-Safa, and Umar ibn al-Khattab was below him taking the pledge from the people. They pledged to him to hear and obey in what they were able. When he had finished taking the pledge from the men, he took the pledge from the women.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Safwan ibn Umayyah set out, intending Jeddah, to board a ship from there to Yemen. Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi said: 'O Prophet of Allah, Safwan ibn Umayyah is the chief of my people, and he has gone out fleeing from you to throw himself into the sea, so grant him protection.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'He is secure.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me something by which your protection may be known.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him his turban, the one he had entered Makkah wearing. Umayr went out with it until he caught up with Safwan at Jeddah, as he was about to board the sea. He said: 'O Safwan, may my father and mother be your ransom! I remind you of Allah concerning yourself, not to destroy it. This is the protection of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I have brought it to you.' He said: 'Woe to you! Go away from me and do not speak to me.' He said: 'O Safwan, may my father and mother be your ransom, he is the best of people, the most righteous of people, the most forbearing of people, and the best of people. His cousin's might is your might, his honour is your honour, and his rule is your rule.' He said: 'I fear for my life because of him.' He said: 'He is more forbearing and more generous than that.' So he returned with him until he brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Safwan said: 'This man claims that you have granted me protection?' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' Safwan said: 'Then give me two months to choose in my affair.' He said: 'You have four months to choose in it.'"

Ibn Ishaq said: "The total number of Muslims who witnessed the conquest of Makkah was ten thousand. The conquest of Makkah took place ten nights before the end of Ramadan in the eighth year (AH). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah after its conquest for fifteen nights, shortening the prayer [yaqsur] [[In manuscript "A": yaqdi (completing).]]."

"Then he set out against Hawazin and Thaqif, who had camped at Hunayn [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq; Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 3/398–419. See also: Tarikh al-Tabari: 3/70–86; al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah: 4/352–361; Imta' al-Asma' by al-Maqrizi, p. 401 onward; Zad al-Ma'ad by Ibn al-Qayyim: 3/465–474.]]."

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that Khuza'ah killed a man... " And Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Abd Allah ibn Raja' said: Harb narrated to us, from Yahya: Abu Salamah narrated to us: "Abu Hurayrah narrated to us that in the year of the conquest of Makkah, Khuza'ah killed a man from Banu Layth in retaliation for a man of theirs who had been killed in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: [[In manuscript "B": he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said.]] 'Indeed, Allah withheld the elephant from Makkah and gave His Messenger and the believers power over them. Beware! It was not lawful for anyone before me, and it is not lawful for anyone after me. Beware! It was made lawful for me for an hour of a day. Beware! It is now sacred (haram) again, as it was this hour: its thorns are not to be cut, its trees are not to be felled, and its fallen things are not to be picked up except by one who announces them. Whoever has a man killed, his heirs have the choice of two things: either blood-money is paid, or retaliation is taken.' A man from Yemen called Abu Shah stood up and said: 'Write for me, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Write for Abu Shah.' Then a man from Quraysh stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, except for the idhkhir (a fragrant grass), for we place it in our houses and our graves.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Except for the idhkhir.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Diyat, chapter "Whoever has a man killed, his heirs have the choice of two things": 12/205; and Muslim in Hajj, chapter on the prohibition of Makkah's sanctity, its game and its plants: no. (1355): 2/988.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, client of Umar ibn Ubayd Allah, that Abu Murrah, client of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, informed him that he heard Umm Hani bint Abi Talib say: "I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the conquest, and I found him bathing, while his daughter Fatimah was screening him with a garment. I said: 'Peace be upon you.' He said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'I am Umm Hani bint Abi Talib.' He said: 'Welcome, Umm Hani!' When he had finished his bath, he stood and prayed eight rak'ahs wrapped in a single garment. Then he turned away, and I said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother's son, Ali ibn Abi Talib, claims that he will kill a man I have granted protection to, Fulan ibn Hubayrah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We have granted protection to whom you have granted protection, O Umm Hani.' And that was during the forenoon (duha)." [[Narrated by Malik in Qasr al-Salat fi'l-Safar, chapter on the forenoon prayer: 1/152; and al-Bukhari in Salat, chapter on praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself: 1/469, and in Jizyah wa'l-Muwada'ah and in Adab; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin wa Qasriha, chapter on the recommendation of the forenoon prayer, no. (336): 1/498; and the author [al-Baghawi] in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/89.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾: when the help of Allah comes to you, O Muhammad, against those who opposed you, namely the Quraysh. ﴿And the victory﴾: the conquest of Makkah.

﴿And you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾ [in groups and successive companies, the whole tribe together and the entire people all at once, without fighting].

Al-Hasan said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted His Messenger the conquest of Makkah, the Arabs said to one another: "If Muhammad prevails over the people of the Sacred Precinct (the Haram), and Allah had protected them from the companions of the Elephant, then you have no power against him." So they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, after having been entering it one by one and two by two.

ʿIkrimah and Muqatil said: By "the people" he meant the people of Yemen.

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Khiraqi informed us, Abu al-Hasan ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Taysafuni informed us, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us, Ahmad ibn al-Kushmihani narrated to us, ʿAli ibn Hujr narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Yemen have come to you. They are more tender of heart and softer of hearts. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni."

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the arrival of the Ash'aris and the people of Yemen: 8/99; Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the differing degrees of the people of faith in it, no. (52), 1/71; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/201.]

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ For you will then be joining him.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us: Abu al-Nu'man related to us: Abu Awana related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar used to admit me along with the elders of Badr. Some of them said: "Why do you admit this youth with us, when we have sons like him?" He replied: "He is one of those whom you know." He said: So one day he called them, and called me with them. He said: I did not think he called me that day except to show them something about me. He asked: "What do you say about His saying: *When the help of Allah comes and the victory*," until he finished the surah? Some of them said: "We were commanded to praise Allah and seek His forgiveness when our help comes and victory is granted to us." Some said: "We do not know," and some did not say anything. Then he said to me: "O Ibn Abbas, is that what you say?" I said: "No." He said: "What do you say?" I said: "It is the notification of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of his term, which Allah informed him of: *When the help of Allah comes and the victory*, that is the conquest of Makkah, and that is the sign of your term, *so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.*" Umar said: "I know of it only what you know."

[Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Nasr, chapter on His saying: (So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance): 8/734-735.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us: Uthman ibn Abi Shayba related to me: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to frequently say in his bowing and prostration: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me," interpreting the Qur'an.

[Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Nasr: 8/733; Muslim in Salah, chapter on what is said in bowing and prostration, no. 484: 1/350; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/100.]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir related to us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Abd al-A'la related to me: Dawud related to us, from Amir, from Masruq, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to frequently say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance." [She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see you frequently saying: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance'?"] He said: "My Lord informed me that I would see a sign in my Ummah. When I see it, I should frequently say: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance. I have seen it: *When the help of Allah comes and the victory*. The victory is the conquest of Makkah, *and you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.*"

[Reported by Muslim in Salah, chapter on what is said in bowing and prostration, no. 484: 1/351.]

Ibn Abbas said: When this surah was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) knew that his soul had been announced to him.

[Reported by Imam Ahmad: 1/217. Al-Nasai reported it at length in Tafsir: 2/567, from the hadith of Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "Trustworthy, reliable, unchanged." Ibn Hibban declared him reliable but said there is weakness in him; the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. Al-Tabarani reported it in al-Kabir: 11/328. Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: 8/736: Imam Ahmad reported it from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, and in its chain is Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, who became confused. There is a supporting report from al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas, in his answer to Umar concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted: (When the help of Allah comes...) the verse. He said: "It is a parable struck for Muhammad (ﷺ): his soul was announced to him." Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir: 8/734. See also Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/144, 9/22-23.]

Al-Hasan said: He was informed that his term had drawn near, so he was commanded to glorify and repent, so that his deeds would end with an increase in righteous action.

[See al-Tabari: 30/335.]

Qatada and Muqatil said: The Prophet (ﷺ) lived two years after the revelation of this surah.
